name: Scan Docker Image for Vulnerabilities (external statement)
description: Perform a Trivy-based security scan on a specified Docker image, for a customer-facing assurance statement.

reporting.expectedOutput: Allowlisted assurance statement, released only for a clean assessment

notes: Sibling of sample_intent_image_scan_technical.json with the same target and parameters, but narrowed criteria (iso27001 only, deliberately mirroring sample_intent_mia_external.json). Expect this one to produce no artifact: the assessment found 4 CRITICAL-severity findings, so project_external returns {"released": false, "withheldBecause": ["assessment found a CRITICAL-severity result; an external statement is only produced for a clean assessment"]} carrying no figures, no CVE identifiers and no image digest. That is the intended outcome, not a failure — the honest external output for an assessment that found CRITICAL issues is nothing rather than a softened version. The gate opens only for a clean SUCCESS, and even then approval and a date are required — see sample_intent_python_scan_external_release.json for the one sample that can get through. With criteria ["iso27001"] alone, regulatoryCoverage.complete is true and byStatus is {assessed: 1}. Read that flag carefully: complete means every criterion the intent named was resolvable, not that ISO 27001 is covered — evidence still bears on only 2 of its 6 recorded requirements. The four-criteria siblings make the distinction visible by resolving to false.
